not_affected.disc2_ee011fa833421022b45e0f3e: The advisory describes a bypass of the CVE-2015-5211 RFD protection through a ";jsessionid=" path parameter: the fixed 4.3.29/5.x code must strip the session id before the RFD content-disposition check runs. At 4.1.1 neither half exists: UrlPathHelper.removeSemicolonContent (spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/web/util/UrlPathHelper.java:454-478) drops all ";" content in the default removeSemicolonContent branch and always removes ";jsessionid=" through removeJsessionid in the disabled branch, and the RFD protection (addContentDispositionHeader in RequestResponseBodyMethodProcessor) was only added by the CVE-2015-5211 fix, after this snapshot. The 2020 fix eb11c6fa2330 reinstates exactly the jsessionid removal that 4.1.1 already performs, so the bypass mechanism does not exist here; the underlying RFD issue is the separately tracked CVE-2015-5211 row.
not_affected.disc2_8664d76e6cee9921f0c70d27: The advisory describes unbounded growth of a SpEL pattern cache. That cache is the parser-level ConcurrentMap/ConcurrentLruCache introduced by the CVE-2023-20861 fix in 5.2.23; at 4.1.1 OperatorMatches.getValueInternal calls Pattern.compile((String) right) inline (spring-expression/src/main/java/org/springframework/expression/spel/ast/OperatorMatches.java:67) and no pattern, expression or AST cache exists in the spring-expression module, so there is no cache whose growth can exhaust memory. The 6.2.19 fix e8f08b415849/ec89834fa8f6 bounds the cache (MAX_PATTERN_CACHE_SIZE = 256) that a later release introduced, which is a regression fix for 5.2.23+ code, not a pre-image present at 4.1.1.

left_open.disc2_ac9c5df2a03d6b22e63af912: Vendor page scope is "5.3.48 and earlier", so 4.1.1.RELEASE is nominally inside the affected range, but the only published fix is 5.3.49 Enterprise Support Only; there is no public commit, the v5.3.48/v5.3.49 tags are not public, and no source hunk shows where the SpEL integer overflow is. The CWE-190 defect cannot be located by static review at 4.1.1 without the fix diff, so the row stays open rather than being promoted or refuted.

notes: The frozen SHA is the 4.1.1.RELEASE tag commit (2014-10-01); the cached source is a shallow single-commit clone, so all fix hunks were fetched through the GitHub API and compared against a direct read of the frozen tree.

Fourteen rows are promoted with a real 4.1.1 file:line/function anchor. Eleven anchor on code that the 5.2.x/5.3.x/6.1.x/6.2.x fixes change; CVE-2016-1000027 (removal at 6.0.0) and CVE-2022-22970 (guard rewritten by 50177b1ad3) are anchored on a direct source review of the sink the advisory names.

The vendor pages for the 2026-418xx batch list "5.3.48 and earlier", which includes 4.1.1.RELEASE. The GHSA-parsed text narrows some of them to "5.3.0 through 5.3.48"; where the two disagree the vendor page is used and the GHSA range is recorded in the row.
CVE-2026-41849 stays open: its vendor range covers 4.1.1 but the only fix is 5.3.49 Enterprise and no public commit reveals the CWE-190 overflow site.

CVE-2020-5421 is closed not affected because its jsessionid bypass targets the CVE-2015-5211 RFD check that 4.1.1 does not have; CVE-2026-41851 is closed not affected because the unbounded pattern cache it describes was introduced in 5.2.23 and no cache exists at 4.1.1.

Severity levels and vectors are taken verbatim from the GHSA database_specific severity and CVSS_V3 vector; no numeric base score is derived here, so severity.status stays unknown unless a publisher score exists in the record.
